subject: Alleyway SDK Gateway v1 deprecation — coordination and migration matrix
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@alleyway.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Partner Success <ps@alleyway.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Alleyway SDK Gateway v1 deprecation — compatibility ask

Hi Kimberly,

Quick heads up from Alleyway: we plan to deprecate the Alleyway -> Redwood Gateway v1 integration that our SDKs still call by default. The rough target is EOL ~Q4 2026 (we're proposing Nov 30, 2026 as the date). Before we finalize, we wanted to coordinate with your SDK/runtime teams so we can publish a clear migration matrix and avoid customer breakage.

What we need from Redwood: 
- A compatibility/versioning matrix showing which Redwood runtime versions and model variants will accept the new Gateway v2 tokens/capabilities.
- Any breaking changes in request/response contract (headers, streaming framing, error codes).
- A recommended migration window and whether Redwood can provide a backward-compat shim for at least one release cycle.
- Contact and a list of customers you think may be impacted (so Alleyway can prioritize adaptors).

We'd like to propose a joint migration sprint (2 weeks) with a short canary phase and a controlled cutoff. Attached is a short impact overview from our side.

Can we book 30 minutes this week to sync? Proposed times: Wed 8/26 10:00–11:00 PDT or Thu 8/27 14:00–15:00 PDT.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

— Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Platform Partnerships
Alleyway AI
[Attachment: alleyway_migration_impact_overview.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@alleyway.ai>
Cc: Partner Success <ps@alleyway.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Alleyway SDK Gateway v1 deprecation — compatibility ask

Maya — thanks for the heads up and for the attachment. We should definitely coordinate to avoid surprises for customers. I can take point from Redwood's side for the partnership coordination.

Action items I need from Alleyway ahead of any sprint:
- A concrete list of SDKs/adaptors that will emit v1 vs v2 traffic (language + versions).
- A proposed deprecation timeline with hard dates and any flexibility.
- Any test vectors or a small test harness (postman collection / sample payloads) to exercise the new protocol behaviors (streaming/error cases).

From Redwood's side we'll:
- Pull a short list of customers who use Alleyway adaptors and surface criticality.
- Run a compatibility pass between your matrix and our runtime teams (runtime@redwood.com) — need a mapping of endpoints and expected error codes.
- Discuss feasibility of a temporary shim layer (our SDK team tends to avoid long shims but can consider a 1-release bridge).

My team is available Wed 8/26 10:00 PDT — locking that as the working sync unless you prefer Thu. I've looped in Marcus Lin (Partner Engineering) and Vanessa Ortiz (SDK PM) to the thread so we can coordinate the technical side and schedule engineering time.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Alleyway SDK Gateway v1 deprecation — coordination and migration matrix

Kim / Vanessa — forwarding Alleyway's note. Quick internal summary / ask: 

Summary: Alleyway plans to EOL their Gateway v1 integration and wants Redwood to produce a compatibility matrix + consider a shim for one release cycle. They propose Nov 30, 2026 as EOL and want a joint migration sprint + canary.

Questions for runtime/SDK owners (please reply inline):
1) Do we have a produced mapping today that ties runtime build versions (e.g., 2026.06, 2026.08) to accepted auth tokens / framing? If not, estimate effort to produce one (docs + test vectors).
2) Are there any planned runtime changes (Q3/Q4 releases) that would block a shim or make v2 mandatory earlier?
3) If we offer a backward-compatible shim, what SLA / maintenance burden do we accept? (suggest: support shim for one release cycle = ~90 days).

Preliminary internal proposal:
- Schedule sync Wed 8/26 10:00 PDT (Kim locked this).
- Alleyway provides language-specific SDK list and test harness by EOD Mon 8/31.
- Redwood delivers a draft compatibility matrix and short migration guide by Fri 9/11.
- Joint canary window mid-Oct, full cutover target Nov 30.

Risks: large enterprise customers using older adaptors could need additional time; licensing/legal constraints if token formats change.

Assigning owners: Vanessa — SDK PM to review adaptor surface and estimate shim cost. Vanessa, can you confirm engineering availability for Sept/Oct?

— Marcus
Partner Engineering

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@alleyway.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Partner Success <ps@alleyway.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Alleyway SDK Gateway v1 deprecation — compatibility ask

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround. Wed 8/26 10:00 PDT works for Alleyway — I'll send a calendar invite. Per Kim/Marcus requests, attached are two artifacts: a proposed timeline (proposed_timeline.pdf) and a migration matrix spreadsheet (migration_matrix_v1.xlsx) that lists the SDK packages, versions, and suggested adaptor changes. Key excerpts below: 

- Proposed timeline (high level):
  * 2026-09-01: Alleyway publishes SDK updates that default to Gateway v2 but keep v1 flag for opt-in.
  * 2026-10-15—11-15: Joint canary window (we will coordinate customer subsets).
  * 2026-11-30: Target EOL for v1.

- Migration matrix (excerpt):
  * alleyway-js 2.x -> requires header X-AW-Gateway: v2 or fallback param 'aw_gw=2'
  * alleyway-python 1.8.x -> client-level flag enable_gateway_v2=True + new streaming framing (small payload ordering change).
  * alleyway-dotnet 3.1 -> requires server TLS SNI validation for v2 tokens.

We can provide a small Postman collection and a dockerized test harness that emits both v1 and v2 traffic against a Redwood staging endpoint. Will attach link in the invite.

For customers impacted: Alleyway will share the list of customers using older adaptors — but we'd appreciate Redwood's feedback on which of those are strategic / high-risk so we can sequence canaries.

Attachments: proposed_timeline.pdf, migration_matrix_v1.xlsx

See you on the call.

— Maya
Head of Platform Partnerships, Alleyway AI
